mcat_description.short: A prefabricated, ventilated enclosure designed to isolate tobacco smokers in workplaces, airports, hospitality venues, and public spaces, preventing smoke migration to non-smoking areas. Sold as a complete modular unit with integrated exhaust/filtration systems, fire-resistant panels, and optional amenities.
mcat_description.long: Smoking cabins are factory-built, self-contained structures engineered to create designated smoking zones that comply with public health and workplace safety regulations. They incorporate high-efficiency mechanical ventilation or air filtration systems that maintain negative pressure relative to adjacent areas, ensuring exhaust air is discharged outside and not recirculated. Construction typically uses fire-resistant wall panels (steel, GI, or composite), integrated smoke detectors, and optional features such as benches, ashtrays, lighting, and climate control. Buyers are primarily facility managers, corporate campuses, airports, hospitality groups, and industrial plant operators procuring a turnkey compliance solution rather than a raw building material.

market_context: Smoking cabins in the Indian B2B market are prefabricated, ventilated enclosures procured by facility managers and EHS officers to comply with public health regulations that prohibit smoking in enclosed public spaces (Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products Act, COTPA 2003, and its amendments). The dominant commercial form is a fully enclosed, mechanically ventilated cabin with negative-pressure exhaust, fire-resistant panel construction, and integrated amenities (benches, ashtrays, lighting). Indian manufacturers such as Texo Prefab World supply these as turnkey units; international brands like Euromate (Smoke 'n Go series) are also present in the Indian market through distributors. Key buyer vocabulary includes 'designated smoking area,' 'smoking zone cabin,' and 'ventilated smoking room.' A significant contamination risk exists in this MCAT: food/rubber smokehouses (used for curing meat, fish, or rubber sheets) share the keyword 'smokehouse' and appear in IndiaMART listings under this category — these are industrial processing equipment with a completely different buyer and working principle and must be routed to food processing or rubber processing equipment MCATs. Standard booth sizes range from compact single-person units to multi-person modular rooms; no dominant Indian BIS standard specific to smoking cabins was identified (single source — low confidence), though fire safety (NBC 2016) and ventilation norms apply.
